summary: Bootstrap 'Model Integration Sandbox' Jira project + Slack alias with ephemeral guest flow and AD-group sync
description:
Issue summary:
We need a new standardized internal project template called 'Model Integration Sandbox' that provisions a scoped Jira project, an associated Confluence space seeded with a template, and a Slack alias/namespace for ephemeral guest collaboration. The flow should include AD group sync for guest access, automated channel archival after TTL, and a lightweight service-account rotation hook for the provisioning automation.

Impact:
- Currently teams create ad-hoc sandboxes with inconsistent retention and access controls — increases audit surface and onboarding friction for external collaborators.
- This blocks small partner integrations and experiment work that needs short-lived external reviewers.

Request details / desired behavior:
1) New Jira project template 'Model Integration Sandbox' (project key autogenerated SAND?) with the following defaults:
   - Issue types: Task, Bug, Experiment, Onboarding Checklist
   - Workflow: simplified triage -> in progress -> review -> closed
   - Default labels: sandbox, integration, external-review
2) Confluence space seeded from a specific internal template (Integration README + Security checklist + Data handling stub) and an owner field that points to a team rotation group.
3) Slack alias/namespace: a short prefix (e.g., #mi-<project>) created when project is instantiated; channel creation flow auto-provisions three channels: mi-<id>-general, mi-<id>-transcripts, mi-<id>-actions.
4) Ephemeral guest access flow: allow external guests to be invited for a TTL of 14 days by the rotating owner group; AD group sync must provision group membership and remove access when TTL expires.
5) Archival and export: mi-*-transcripts channel should have an automated nightly export (thread transcripts) to the Confluence space with a timestamped page and redaction hooks for PII flagged by a simple regex filter.
6) Service account/service token rotation: the automation must use an L2 service account with documented rotation every 30 days and KMS-backed secrets.
7) Audit hooks: every provisioning event must log a Jira comment and write an entry to the internal provisioning audit Confluence page and to the admin Slack channel #ops-provisioning.

Acceptance criteria:
- Teams can use a self-serve UI or Jira button to instantiate a sandbox and see all three artifacts (Jira project, Confluence space, Slack alias) created within 10 minutes.
- Guest invites are scoped to TTL and are automatically removed by AD sync at TTL expiry.
- Transcript export appears in Confluence and is readable to owners; PII redaction removes simple email/SSN patterns.
- Provisioning events are logged and visible in #ops-provisioning.

Timeline / urgency:
- Low-medium urgency: would be valuable for upcoming partner experiments in Q2 2026. Request pilot by 2026-04-15.

Notes / constraints:
- Security should review the redaction approach before pilot; do not enable exports for any project classified as regulated without explicit approval.
- Avoid creating new Slack apps without Security approval; prefer reuse of existing provisioning bot if feasible.
steps_to_validate: 1) From the provisioning UI, select 'Model Integration Sandbox' and start a new instance. 2) Confirm Jira project appears with the expected issue types and labels. 3) Confirm Confluence space exists and the template page is present. 4) Confirm Slack channels (mi-<id>-general, -transcripts, -actions) are created and the alias/preview is visible. 5) Invite an external guest and verify they are added to an AD group with TTL metadata. 6) Wait forced TTL expiry or run the AD-sync job and confirm guest is removed. 7) Post a threaded conversation in mi-<id>-transcripts, run export, and verify Confluence page content with redactions.
investigation_notes:
Initial feasibility check by Platform Ops (2026-03-10):
- Provisioning bot can create Jira projects and Confluence spaces via API; Slack channel creation currently requires an admin-scoped token in workspace context.
- AD group sync exists for hires but not generalized for ephemeral guest groups; may need extension of the existing directory-syncer service.
- Transcript export will rely on the conversation-export Lambda (PR 1234) but needs redaction layer; suggested approach: run regex passes then surface original to Sec-only review if flagged.
- KMS integration for service-account rotation already exists; adapt existing rotation schedule endpoint.
